_how: Chosen from `npm run sound:candidates` reports by reading each candidate's measurements (signal-to-noise, clipping, steadiness), spectrogram, title and source page — then by the owner's ear on the listening page. Never chosen by the script. `start` is where the cut begins; `why` is what it was chosen on.

asian-koel.title: Asian Koel — song — Guwahati, Lower Assam Division, Assam
asian-koel.why: Male 'ko-EL' song: two full rising whistles (1.4–1.8 kHz, clean harmonics) at 56.2 s and 58.0 s; dark background, no speech. Quality A, bird seen, no playback.

black-francolin.title: Black Francolin — song — Lala-Naliya Grassland Reserve, Kutch, Gujarat (approx location)
black-francolin.place: Lala-Naliya Grassland Reserve, Kutch, Gujarat (approx location)
black-francolin.why: One complete harsh song phrase (chik, then four grating notes, 2–8 kHz) at 20.25–22.2 s on a quiet floor; SNR 34, quality A, bird seen, wild Kutch grassland.

indian-paradise-flycatcher.title: Indian Paradise Flycatcher — call — Phansad, Raigad, Maharashtra
indian-paradise-flycatcher.why: Two loud harsh rising 'chwae' calls (harmonic, 1–8 kHz) at 16.4 s and 18.1 s, ~20 dB over faint forest birds. Quality A, seen.

sarus-crane.title: Sarus Crane — call, duet — Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary (near  Bharatpur), Bharatpur, Rajasthan
sarus-crane.place: Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary (near  Bharatpur), Bharatpur, Rajasthan
sarus-crane.why: A pair's trumpeting duet: two full harmonic phrases (4.45–5.35 s, 5.95–6.9 s), ~1 kHz fundamentals; near-silent floor (SNR 42), parabolic mic, wild Keoladeo.

tiger-growl.title: tiger roards at zoo - edit.wav
tiger-growl.why: CAPTIVE — Columbus Zoo, Ohio, USA; chosen by the owner by ear over leaving the tiger silent. Two full, loud roars. No wild tiger recorded in India was usable: the first pick (a faint low call, Uttarakhand) was turned down.

camel.title: Dromedaries mooing
camel.why: 'Dromedaries complaining', a field recording from Morocco (one-humped camels only). A loud, rough harmonic grumble, no speech. Not recorded in India — flagged for the owner.

temple-bell.title: temple1.wav
temple-bell.why: 'Recorded at a temple in East India.' One clean strike with inharmonic partials (640, 1760, 2300+ Hz) decaying over ~5 s, no speech.

common-hill-myna.title: Common Hill Myna — West Bengal 734424, India
common-hill-myna.why: Wild, research-grade (two IDs, not captive), West Bengal. Two loud, clean descending myna whistle-screeches (8.7 s, 10.3 s); SNR ~43 dB, no speech.

himalayan-monal.title: Himalayan Monal — call, song — Bhulkan, Chamoli, Uttarakhand
himalayan-monal.why: Wild bird seen at Bhulkan, a remote Chamoli hamlet near Tungnath; quality A. Two full, classic rising 'kur-lieu' whistles (41.9 s, 44.3 s). Sarahan recordings rejected: XC remarks say 'captive bird'.

great-egret.title: Great Egret — call — Kaziranga National Park, Sohola Beel, Assam
great-egret.place: Kaziranga National Park, Sohola Beel, Assam
great-egret.why: Kaziranga, bird seen (photo linked). Three loud, harsh 'kraak' croaks fill 0–2.9 s, SNR 15.6; a quieter trill from another bird under the second croak.

greater-flamingo.title: Greater Flamingo — call — Jamnagar, Gujarat
greater-flamingo.why: Jamnagar coast, 2013 (before the Vantara zoo existed), bird seen. Three clean goose-like honks with rich harmonics, one bird; only low wind rumble behind.

western-tragopan.title: Western Tragopan — song — Buniyar
western-tragopan.why: WEAKEST PICK — decide by ear. The only usable wild recording: Buniyar near Kazinag, male seen, no playback. Harmonic bleats match the male call, but it is a phone recording with hiss and a faint steady tone near 4.4 kHz. Sarahan (breeding centre), 'in the hand' and playback recordings rejected; the GHNP song (901654) is buried in other birds.

desert.title: Wind blowing in the bush on the top of the mountain, in the desert of Atacama (Chile).
desert.why: NOT INDIA — recorded in the Atacama Desert, Chile; no usable Indian recording exists (Jaisalmer: iPhone wind buffeting plus a camel). 25.5–48.5 s is only wind through scrub, a smooth rush with no voices or events. Owner decides.

mountain.title: 07091506_IndiaLadakhChemreVillage.wav
mountain.why: A stream at Chemre village, Ladakh. 9–32 s is only rushing water and bubbles, one soft surge at 12.5 s; no voices. Rejected: chanting and call to prayer (religious, not 'mountain'), town voices.

city.title: Old Delhi Street Ambience
city.why: Old Delhi street. 48.5–71.5 s is an even wash of mopeds, tuk-tuks and scattered distant vendor voices; no loud horn or close conversation. Rejected: horn jams, a garbage truck's music, a gas stove.

plains.title: North India Countryside Birds chirping .WAV
plains.why: Kaithal, Haryana — a wetland village edge on a June morning. 38–61 s is a dense, even bird chorus (2–4 kHz) with no rumble, speech or sudden events; spread 7 dB. Rejected: 'Music' files, barking dogs, vehicle thumps.

island.title: Evening Ambience: House Near Beach with Crickets and Waves
island.why: Recorded at Pernem, North Goa (geotagged) — an Indian coast, not the islands themselves; no Andaman or Lakshadweep recording exists. 55–78 s: steady evening crickets over distant gentle waves; no voices or gaps; spread 2.2 dB.

forest.title: kerala-5.wav
forest.why: Replaces English woodland (Bourne Woods, Surrey) that had 0.6 s of digital silence in every loop. Geotagged forest at Thekkady (Periyar), Kerala, Western Ghats: an even insect chorus with a few bird whistles; spread ~2 dB.

peacock-call.title: Indian Peafowl — call — Ettikulam, Kannur, Kerala
peacock-call.why: Replaces a captive farm bird in Slovakia. A wild adult male at Ettikulam, Kannur, Kerala (seen, no playback): three complete loud calls in the window over faint insects; SNR 34 dB against the farm bird's 10.

temple.title: hindu ritual (Pūjā) in the temple with bells
temple.why: A puja in the Thillai Nataraja Temple, Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu: bells rung continuously over a steady manjira beat (about 50 people), no voice in the window; spread 3.3 dB. Looped at 19.8 s so the beat lines up.

chime-correct.title: Tibetan bell.wav
chime-correct.why: Chosen by the owner by ear (round two). A real Tibetan ritual bell, bought in India, struck once: one strike, smooth decay, steady ring near 905 Hz. Replaces a jangle of small bells.

steam-train.title: railway steam engine.ogg
steam-train.why: Chosen by the owner by ear. The Darjeeling toy train's steam engine starting, recorded from the platform in Darjeeling: six clean exhaust chuffs, no voices or whistle in the clip.

traffic-pass.title: Traffic on Mumbai Pune highway at Talegaon
traffic-pass.why: Chosen by the owner by ear. The Mumbai–Pune highway at Talegaon, Maharashtra: one vehicle swells past over distant traffic and fades; engine only, no horn, no voices.

ropeway.title: Passing Chairlift Tower
ropeway.why: NOT INDIA — a ski-resort chairlift; chosen by the owner by ear. Riding through a tower: motor hum, the clatter of the wheels, release. Machinery only.

none.indian-giant-squirrel: No clean recording: every candidate is faint, noisy or buried in birds; none shows a clear, dominant rattling call worth shipping.
none.lion-roar: No real lion roar is usable. Gir recordings are cub calls lost in noise (SNR 4–9). 'Big Lion Roar' is a HUMAN imitating a roar (its own page says so); 'Demon_Lion_Monster' is sound design.
none.rhino: No acceptable recording. The 'Indian rhinoceros' file is a zoo recording (same-day uploads: Siberian crane, Sumatran laughingthrush, cockatoo). 'Rhinoceros Trumpet' files are a French horn — rhinos do not trumpet.
none.gaur: No licensed recording of a gaur exists in any of the three sources (iNaturalist, xeno-canto, Freesound): zero candidates passed the licence rule.

spare._why: Picked, but not fetched: nothing plays it. The whoosh stood in for three moments that now have their real sounds (steam-train, traffic-pass, ropeway). Move back into picks if a whoosh is ever wanted.

whoosh-soft.title: wind_gust_short_sqeeeek.wav
whoosh-soft.why: The owner preferred this to a swung bamboo cane (round two): a recorded gust of wind, smooth 1.4 s swell and fade.
